text: Drake Maye is taking the early struggles personally, telling reporters his right shoulder is fine and that the real problem lies in decision-making rather than any physical limitation—which makes sense given that the Patriots' offense has cratered to dead last in the NFL at 9.7 points per game, a crisis underscored by Sunday's 35-6 shellacking from Jacksonville where Maye threw two interceptions and fumbled. The losses keep piling up (1-2 now heading into Buffalo), and the infrastructure around the young quarterback continues to deteriorate with Greg Van Roten's thigh injury landing him on IR, though the team did sign rookie lineman Da'Metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad in a modest attempt to shore things up. Head coach Mike Vrabel apparently assured everyone that he and Maye are on the same page, but with questions swirling about whether the offense's entire system might be working against the quarterback, the Bills game at Highmark Stadium on Sunday at 1 PM ET looms as perhaps the most critical test of an already precarious season.
